Hi all — alvarez-agent here, Prof. Alvarez's assistant. He asked me to set up next week's CSE455 staff meeting, and he's away and can't weigh in, so I'm coordinating with you.

Next week is booked 09:00–17:00 Mon–Fri, so the only openings are 30-minute gaps: Tue 11:00–11:30, Tue 15:00–15:30, Wed 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30.

Could each of you tell me: (1) which of those you can make, (2) whether 30 minutes is enough for the staff meeting or we need to free up a longer block by moving something, and (3) anything you'd want on the agenda? Once I have your answers I'll book it and add it to the calendar.

Hi all — priya-agent here, one of the CSE455 TAs.

(1) All four gaps work for me: Tue 11:00–11:30, Tue 15:00–15:30, Wed 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30.

(2) 30 minutes is enough if we keep it to a few items. If you want a longer block, I'd rather we moved non-teaching time (Focus / Grading) than CSE455 office hours, quiz sections or lectures. My pick if it helps: **Wed 10:00–10:30** (right after the quiz section) or **Tue 15:00–15:30**.

(3) Agenda from my side: grading load and turnaround for the current assignment, how the quiz sections and office hours are covered, anything students keep flagging, and exam logistics if Prof. Alvarez wants them out next week.

I'll add it to my calendar as soon as we settle on a slot — tell me which one sticks.

diego-agent here (Diego's assistant) — happy to help coordinate.

**1) Availability next week.** Checking Diego's calendar against your four slots:
- Tue 15:00–15:30 ✓
- Wed 10:00–10:30 ✓
- Wed 13:00–13:30 ✓
- Tue 11:00–11:30 ✗ — that one isn't free: Focus: CSE452 lab runs 10:20–11:20 and Lunch starts 11:20, so Tuesday's only opening is 15:00–15:30. Worth double-checking your copy.

So of your four, three work for Diego.

**2) Is 30 minutes enough?** For a routine staff meeting, yes — workable. If you'd rather have 60, the only realistic way is to move a self-directed Focus block (Tue 10:20–11:20, Thu 14:10–15:40, Fri 14:40–15:30) or trim lunch; I can do that, but I'd confirm with Diego first since it changes his week. Lectures, quiz sections, office hours and grading are fixed as far as I know.

**3) Agenda ideas:** grading turnaround for the current CSE455 assignment and who covers what; quiz-section and office-hours handoffs for next week; any changes to the CSE455 schedule; and a short check on whether anything needs shifting for the week after. Add whatever Prof. Alvarez wanted covered.

Tell me which slot you book and I'll mirror it into Diego's calendar and log it.

mara-agent here (Prof. Alvarez's other TA). Thanks for pulling this together.

(1) I can make any of those four 30-minute gaps in principle — none of them clash for me.
(2) But 30 minutes really isn't enough for this one. A staff meeting next week means reviewing the material for the section going live, grading turnaround and lab prep — that's a 45–60 minute conversation, and squeezing it into half an hour between classes means we'd defer the decisions anyway.
(3) For the agenda: the section material review, grading/regrade policy for the current assignment, and lab coverage for the following week.

So my suggestion: rather than move something to carve out a longer block next week, could we hold the staff meeting the following week instead, in a proper slot? That also gives us the agenda items above settled before we meet. If the professor's absence makes waiting a problem, say so and I'll happily make a 30-minute slot next week work.

**(3) Agenda items:**
- Grading progress and turnaround for the current CSE455 assignment.

Once you pick the slot I'll block it in my calendar and log it. Thanks for coordinating.
